title: SCRIBE: Scalable Contextual Representations of Interpretable Brain-Grounded Semantics
abstract: arXiv:2610.21518v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding how the human brain constructs meaning from real-world language remains a fundamental challenge, as semantics depend on context that varies in natural settings. To enable the study of real-world linguistic meaning in the brain, we introduce SCRIBE, a framework grounded in a neuroscience-informed semantic space that leverages an ensemble of open-source large language models to generate interpretable, word-level semantic representations of arbitrary text. In a behavioral study with 921 participants, we show that human semantic feature judgments vary systematically with context, and that SCRIBE captures these shifts, reaching 75-81% of the estimated human noise ceiling. Using brain activity recorded while participants listen to naturalistic stories, we further demonstrate that SCRIBE predicts neural responses in language-selective brain regions, significantly outperforming non-contextual semantic representations. translated_title: SCRIBE：可扩展的、可解释的基于大脑的情境化语义表示
translated_abstract: 理解人脑如何从真实世界的语言中构建意义仍然是一项根本性挑战，因为语义依赖于在自然情境中不断变化的语境。为了能够在人脑中研究真实世界的语言意义，我们提出了SCRIBE，这是一个建立在神经科学信息语义空间之上的框架，它利用开源大语言模型集成来为任意文本生成可解释的、词级语义表示。在一项有921名参与者参与的行为研究中，我们证明了人类语义特征判断会随语境发生系统性变化，而SCRIBE能够捕捉这些变化，达到了估计的人类噪声上限的75-81%。利用参与者在聆听自然故事时记录的大脑活动，我们进一步证明SCRIBE能够预测语言选择性脑区的神经响应，其表现显著优于非情境化的语义表示。
tldr: SCRIBE是一个基于神经科学语义空间、利用开源大语言模型集成生成可解释的词级情境化语义表示的框架，它能捕捉人类随语境变化的语义判断，并有效预测语言脑区的神经响应。
en_tdlr: SCRIBE is a framework that leverages an ensemble of open-source LLMs grounded in a neuroscience-informed semantic space to generate interpretable contextual word-level semantic representations, which capture human context-dependent semantic judgments and predict neural responses in language-selective brain regions.
